name: Dee
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dee, called Deva by the Romans, was a British goddess. Her name means 'the goddess' and was borne by the River Dee. Like most rivers in Celtic lands, she was thought to be a feminine divine force. The River Dee was believed to need regular human victims. A folk rhyme said that 'Bloodthirsty Dee, each year needs three; but bonny Don, she needs none.' The Romans named her from their own word for goddess, Deva.
objective: Records the River Dee as a British goddess who demanded regular human victims.
key_results: Dee's name means 'the goddess' and the Romans called the river Deva.
